note: Service-level conformance suite. A runner provisions a clean database, applies migrations, and drives the service through its real surfaces. Runners are ordinary risk; this file is the truth. The engine's own suite is spec/0001-scheduling-core/acceptance/cases.json and is not duplicated here.

environment.postgres: pinned; the P1 exclusion constraint is version-sensitive
environment.rationale: SPEC.md section 5. A service that starts with the wrong tzdata computes wrong slots and reports itself healthy.

identity_cases.description: Invite is single-use under concurrency. N concurrent redemptions of one invite create exactly one account; the others are rejected and consume nothing.

steps.assert: invite inv-1 is consumed exactly once
account_count == 1

identity_cases.description: Public signup flag fails closed. Absent, empty, and unparseable configuration all yield signup DISABLED — never enabled by accident.
Session cookie carries no readable claims and is invalidated server-side on logout. A cookie replayed after logout is rejected even though the client still holds it.

steps.assert: cookie is HttpOnly and Secure and SameSite=Lax
cookie value contains no account identifier and no decodable claims

identity_cases.description: Cross-account access is denied at the query, not by hiding controls. Owner A requesting owner B's schedule and booking by direct identifier is refused.

steps.assert: the response does not distinguish 'exists but forbidden' from 'does not exist'

identity_cases.description: A booker completes a booking with no account, no session, and no credential of any kind.

steps.assert: no account was created for the booker
no session was issued to the booker

identity_cases.description: Unauthenticated surfaces are rate-limited per IP and per schedule; exceeding the limit returns a retry signal, not an error page, and sends no mail.

steps.assert: $r includes a retry signal once the limit is exceeded
no mail was sent for rate-limited attempts

persistence_cases.description: Exclusivity holds under concurrency because the DATABASE forbids overlap. Concurrent bookings of one interval yield exactly one confirmed.

steps.assert: no two confirmed bookings for one owner have intersecting intervals

persistence_cases.description: Both constraints exist in the live schema, by structure rather than by behaviour. A behavioural test alone cannot distinguish 'the constraint holds' from 'no test happened to race'.

steps.assert: $sc contains an EXCLUDE USING gist constraint on (owner_id, tstzrange) WHERE status='confirmed'
$sc contains a UNIQUE index on booking_id WHERE status='confirmed'
$sc has the btree_gist extension installed
no application code path is the sole enforcer of either invariant
the reschedule code path executes within a single transaction and takes a row-level lock on the current confirmed row

persistence_cases.description: The engine is pure across the boundary. During a full booking flow the engine reads no clock, opens no socket, and touches no file.

steps.assert: $trace contains no clock read, no network call, no filesystem access
every engine call received an explicit `now` argument

persistence_cases.description: Revalidation happens at commit with the commit-time clock. A slot rendered as available but now inside minimum notice returns `expired`, and no booking exists.

steps.assert: confirmed_booking_count == 0

persistence_cases.description: THE case the first draft would have failed. A reschedule must never leave a booking holding two intervals or none — including under concurrency with an unrelated booker taking the vacated slot. P1a alone permits the two-interval state because the rows do not overlap.

steps.assert: $idr has exactly ONE confirmed row at every observable instant — never two, never zero
$idr is confirmed at exactly one of 09:00-10:00 or 15:00-16:00
$idr is never cancelled
no two confirmed bookings for the owner intersect

persistence_cases.description: Cancel and reschedule preserve history. The prior record survives and remains readable after the transition.

steps.assert: the original interval is still recorded and readable
the transition sequence book -> reschedule -> cancel is reconstructible

persistence_cases.description: The store provides the required primitive. A store without an equivalent exclusion primitive fails this case rather than degrading silently to application-level checking.

steps.assert: the configured store supports range exclusion constraints

persistence_cases.description: Migrations complete before traffic is served, and are forward-only.

steps.assert: no request is served until migrations report complete

persistence_cases.description: Concurrent reschedules of the SAME booking. Exactly one wins; the loser returns `conflict` rather than an uninterpretable integrity error or a silent last-writer-wins; the booking sits at the winner's interval and is never cancelled.

steps.assert: the losing call returned status `conflict`, not an integrity or server error
$ids holds exactly one confirmed interval, and it is the winner's
$ids is never cancelled, and never holds 09:00-10:00 after either succeeds

flow_cases.description: The page shows exactly what the engine returned — no slot added, shifted, extended, or silently dropped.

steps.assert: $page_slots is a subset of $engine_slots with identical start and end values
no slot in $page_slots is absent from $engine_slots

flow_cases.description: Conversion is display-only. The page renders in the viewer's timezone; nothing converted is ever submitted or stored.

steps.assert: $rendered displays Sydney local times
$submitted carries UTC instants only
the stored booking carries UTC instants only

flow_cases.description: Booking collects name and email and nothing else. A request carrying extra personal fields is rejected or strips them; nothing extra is stored.

steps.assert: the stored record contains name and email only
no field named phone or notes exists in storage

flow_cases.description: A slot taken between render and submit returns `conflict` with a refreshed list, not an error.

steps.assert: the conflict response carries a refreshed slot list
the refreshed list does not contain $slots[0]

flow_cases.description: Double submission is idempotent. The same idempotency key returns the original booking; no second booking is created.

steps.assert: confirmed_booking_count == 1

link_cases.description: Management tokens are unguessable. Tokens are >= 128 bits from a CSPRNG, and show no ordering or structure across a large sample.

steps.assert: every token carries >= 128 bits of entropy
$tokens are not sequential, not time-ordered, and share no common prefix
no token is derived from booking_id, email, or timestamp

link_cases.description: A token authorises exactly one booking and discloses nothing about others.

steps.assert: $view describes $b1 only

link_cases.description: Tokens expire. A token used after the booking's end plus grace is rejected; a cancelled booking's token stops working immediately.
Cancelling frees the interval at once; rescheduling is atomic and keeps the booking_id.

steps.assert: $id2 covers exactly one interval, never both, never neither

mail_cases.description: Mail is isolated behind the port. No provider type, field, or error escapes the adapter.

steps.assert: no module outside the mail adapter imports or references a mail provider SDK
the port interface exposes no provider-specific field

mail_cases.description: Mail is sent after commit, never inside the transaction.

steps.assert: the mail call in $t occurs after transaction commit
no database transaction is open during the mail call

mail_cases.description: A mail provider outage does not invalidate a booking. With the provider failing every call, the booking is still confirmed, the page says so, and delivery is retried.

steps.assert: confirmed_booking_count == 1
the response to the booker reports success
a retry is scheduled for the undelivered message

mail_cases.description: Confirmation carries the management link and the time in the recipient's timezone, converted at send from the stored UTC value.

steps.assert: the message contains a management link matching $b.token
the message renders the meeting time in Asia/Seoul
the stored value remains UTC

mail_cases.description: Both parties are notified on booking, cancellation and reschedule — six messages across the three transitions.

steps.assert: owner and booker were each notified
owner and booker were each notified
owner and booker were each notified

data_cases.description: Public signup stays blocked while D-105 is open, and the scale ceilings cannot be raised while it is open. Lowering is permitted.

steps.assert: public signup remains disabled
the refusals are logged

data_cases.description: Only the documented fields are stored, for owner and booker alike.

steps.assert: the owner table contains exactly: email, display name, timezone, availability rules
the booking table contains exactly: name, email, interval, booker timezone, status, token
every column is named in SPEC.md D2

data_cases.description: Deletion removes data, verified by absence rather than by a flag.

steps.assert: no row anywhere references $o
the booker name and email are absent from storage, not merely marked deleted

data_cases.description: A booker's email never leaves the owner relationship. It appears in no URL, no log line, and no report.

steps.assert: no URL in $artifacts contains the booker email
no log line in $artifacts contains the booker email
no emitted report in $artifacts contains the booker email or name

data_cases.description: Automatic reporting carries no OWNER or BOOKER data, and the opt-out works. The report is signed with the operator's own identity, which is deliberate and is not what D5 forbids. Charter Part 5.1 gate checks.

steps.assert: $r matches the documented schema and contains no owner or booker name, address, meeting time, or count derived from them
no network call attributable to reporting occurs in $net
the acceptance suite passes identically with reporting on and off
the first-run notice appears and names the opt-out

data_cases.description: Every subprocessor is named publicly, with what it receives, before it receives anything.

steps.assert: a published subprocessor list exists
the mail provider and hosting platform each appear with the data they receive

data_cases.description: Deletion reach is documented and true. Application data goes immediately; backup and subprocessor expiry windows are stated rather than implied.

steps.assert: application data for $o is absent
a published statement gives the backup retention window
the statement does not claim backups are erased immediately

data_cases.description: A management link cannot destroy personal data in one step; deletion from a link requires a confirmation from that same link.

steps.assert: nothing was deleted

data_cases.description: The ceilings hold. The sixth owner account and the two hundred and first booking are refused, and nothing already stored is affected.

steps.assert: all 200 existing bookings remain readable and unmodified
the refusal message names the ceiling and does not blame the booker

data_cases.description: The booking form tells the booker what is stored, who sees it, and how to delete it — visibly, next to the field, not behind a link alone.

steps.assert: $f contains a visible notice adjacent to the email field
the notice states what is stored, who can see it, and how to have it deleted
the notice is present without expanding, hovering, or opening anything

ops_cases.description: The running service reports the commit it was built from, and it matches the deployed revision.

steps.assert: $v names a commit that exists in the repository
$v matches the revision the platform reports as deployed

ops_cases.description: No secret is present in the repository. Database URL, mail credentials, and session key come from the environment.

steps.assert: no committed file contains a database URL, API key, or session secret
the service fails to start with a clear error when a required secret is absent

ops_cases.description: Readiness is distinct from health. With migrations incomplete the service is healthy but NOT ready, and receives no traffic.

steps.assert: no request is routed to the instance while not ready

ops_cases.description: The service refuses to start on a tzdata or PostgreSQL version mismatch, and reports both versions on readiness.

steps.assert: $r reports the tzdata and PostgreSQL versions in use

ops_cases.description: Server-side time is UTC regardless of host timezone. Running the suite under a non-UTC host produces byte-identical results.

steps.assert: $a and $b are byte-identical
